name: University of Southern Denmark
about: SDU is spread across seven towns in the south and west of Denmark, and where you study matters a great deal. Its headquarters and most of its Danish-taught teaching are in Odense, but almost every fully English-taught bachelor's degree sits in Sønderborg, a small town on the island of Als by the German border, or in Vejle, its newest campus and an IT-focused one. SDU is also unusual in how it admits people: an aptitude test called uniTEST is used for quota 2 on nearly all programmes, and SDU openly recommends that everyone sit it, including applicants whose grades would be good enough for quota 1.

notes: Campus is the single biggest decision at SDU, because the towns are genuinely far apart and nothing like each other.

Sønderborg holds eleven of SDU's fifteen fully English-taught bachelor's degrees. It is a small town on the island of Als in the far south of Jutland, closer to Flensburg in Germany than to any large Danish city, and several hours from Copenhagen by train. The campus, Alsion, is a single modern building shared with a concert hall, and the student body there is strongly international — partly because Danish applicants mostly do not move that far south. Mads Clausen's company Danfoss is based next door, which is why so much of the engineering sits here.

Vejle is SDU's newest campus and holds four English-taught degrees, all of them IT. Vejle is a mid-sized town on the east coast of Jutland on the main motorway and rail line, with a cluster of IT employers nearby, so student jobs are realistic.

Odense is SDU's headquarters and Denmark's third-largest city, half an hour from Copenhagen by fast train — but only one fully English-taught bachelor's degree is taught there, Market and Management Anthropology. If you want Odense and you do not speak Danish, your options are almost nil at bachelor level.

SDU also has campuses in Kolding, Esbjerg, Slagelse and Copenhagen. None of them currently offers a fully English-taught bachelor's degree, so they are not options for an IB student who does not read Danish.

Robot Systems (Robotteknologi) in Odense is often assumed to be English-taught. It is not: SDU lists its tuition language as Danish. Robotics in English at SDU means Mechatronics in Sønderborg at bachelor level.

International Business Administration, Language and Culture (Sønderborg and EUF Flensborg) is listed among SDU's international programmes but is excluded here: SDU gives its tuition language as "English, German and Danish" and it requires Danish level A plus German at A or B level. It took only 6 students in 2026.

"All qualified applicants accepted" appears against most of the Sønderborg and Vejle programmes for 2026. That does not remove the entry requirements or the quota 1 GPA floor — it means everyone who met them and applied on time was offered a place.

The gap between expected places and the number actually admitted runs both ways. Mechatronics BSc expected 100 places and admitted 98; Software Engineering in Sønderborg expected 120 and admitted 44; Artificial Intelligence in Vejle expected 30 and admitted 66. Treat the place counts as planning figures, not caps.
A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. SDU repeats this on every programme page: "A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level."

requirements.label: A qualifying upper-secondary examination

officialWording.text: International Baccalaureate (IB) med IB-Course Result på mindst 18 point sidestilles med en gymnasial eksamen, hvis ansøgeren har opnået mindst karakteren 3 i hvert af de 6 fag, der indgår i IB-forløbet. Endvidere skal ansøgeren have gennemført enkeltfag på gymnasialt niveau svarende til overbygning, jf. reglerne om overbygning i højere forberedelseseksamen (hf-eksamen) i lov om gymnasiale uddannelser.

requirements.alternativeRoute: It does not close this one to you. The Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three of them at HL, as equivalent to a qualifying examination for a Danish university bachelor once you have added two successive raises in the level of upper-secondary subjects, at least one of them to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag or as a self-study candidate. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B level are enough. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the other published route.
requirements.note: The rule is national rather than this university's: the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science sets which examinations are adgangsgivende, and every Danish institution applies the same one. Two things about it are easy to get wrong. GSK (gymnasial supplering) cannot be used for this — GSK raises a subject level for someone who already holds a qualifying examination, so it meets a specific subject requirement but never raises the level of the examination itself. And the average used in quota 1 is the one from the first qualifying examination, so a Course Results holder who supplements or retakes is still converted on the original Course Results result.

officialWording.text: What you need to apply for bachelor of engineering programmes. You can apply to a Bachelor of Engineering programme at SDU if you hold the following IB qualifications: IB Diploma. Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results or IB Certificate provided that you have passed all six subjects with a minimum grade of 3, you have at least three subjects at Higher Level (HL).

requirements.note: SDU publishes two different IB rules on one page, and the difference between them is the whole point. For a bachelor's programme it asks a Course candidate to have "supplemented with at least two individual subjects (minimum one at A-level subject and one at B-level subject)". For a Bachelor of Engineering it asks for nothing beyond the six subjects at grade 3 with three at HL. So a Course candidate reaches this programme with the award as it stands, and no hf-enkeltfag are needed. The national order underneath that: the Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points as equal to a two-year hf without overbygning, and an hf without overbygning is adgangsgivende to a diplomingeniør-uddannelse but not to a universitetsbacheloruddannelse. SDU's own Danish list of qualifying examinations says exactly that — "Eksamener, der kun giver adgang til diplomingeniøruddannelser: Højere forberedelseseksamen (hf) uden overbygning aflagt efter gymnasiereformen 2017" — and DTU publishes the same restriction for its own diplomingeniør intake. Two things this does not do. It does not waive the subject requirements below: Mathematics A, English B and Physics B or Geoscience A still bind, and a Course candidate meets them with IB subjects on the same conversion as anybody else. And the 18-point floor given here is the Agency's rather than SDU's: below 18 points, or with any subject at grade 1 or 2, the Course Results are not a qualifying examination at all and no Danish programme is reachable. Grade 3 in all six subjects already puts the subject total at 18, so the two conditions meet in the same place.

officialWording.text: International Baccalaureate (IB) med IB-Course Result på mindst 18 point sidestilles med en gymnasial eksamen, hvis ansøgeren har opnået mindst karakteren 3 i hvert af de 6 fag, der indgår i IB-forløbet. Endvidere skal ansøgeren have gennemført enkeltfag på gymnasialt niveau svarende til overbygning, jf. reglerne om overbygning i højere forberedelseseksamen (hf-eksamen) i lov om gymnasiale uddannelser.

requirements.alternativeRoute: It does not close this one to you. requirements.note: The rule is national rather than this university's: the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science sets which examinations are adgangsgivende, and every Danish institution applies the same one. officialWording.text: What you need to apply for bachelor of engineering programmes. You can apply to a Bachelor of Engineering programme at SDU if you hold the following IB qualifications: IB Diploma. Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results or IB Certificate provided that you have passed all six subjects with a minimum grade of 3, you have at least three subjects at Higher Level (HL).

requirements.note: SDU publishes two different IB rules on one page, and the difference between them is the whole point. For a bachelor's programme it asks a Course candidate to have "supplemented with at least two individual subjects (minimum one at A-level subject and one at B-level subject)". For a Bachelor of Engineering it asks for nothing beyond the six subjects at grade 3 with three at HL. So a Course candidate reaches this programme with the award as it stands, and no hf-enkeltfag are needed. The national order underneath that: the Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points as equal to a two-year hf without overbygning, and an hf without overbygning is adgangsgivende to a diplomingeniør-uddannelse but not to a universitetsbacheloruddannelse. SDU's own Danish list of qualifying examinations says exactly that — "Eksamener, der kun giver adgang til diplomingeniøruddannelser: Højere forberedelseseksamen (hf) uden overbygning aflagt efter gymnasiereformen 2017" — and DTU publishes the same restriction for its own diplomingeniør intake. Two things this does not do. It does not waive the subject requirements below: Mathematics A, English B and Physics B or Geoscience A still bind, and a Course candidate meets them with IB subjects on the same conversion as anybody else. And the 18-point floor given here is the Agency's rather than SDU's: below 18 points, or with any subject at grade 1 or 2, the Course Results are not a qualifying examination at all and no Danish programme is reachable. Grade 3 in all six subjects already puts the subject total at 18, so the two conditions meet in the same place.

Det kræver, at alle 6 IB-fag (3 HL-fag og 3 SL- eller 4 HL-fag og 2 SL-fag) er bestået med mindst karakteren 3. Det betyder, at de har adgang til at søge optagelse på erhvervsakademi- og professionsbacheloruddannelser gennem kvote 1 og 2. Ansøgere med et Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results på mindst 18 point og mindst karakteren 3 i alle fag kan derudover få adgang til en universitetsbacheloruddannelse gennem kvote 1 og 2 ved enten at supplere med enkeltfag efter samme regler som hf’erne eller tage deres IB-eksamen om for at få et IB Diploma – Retake.

notes: 30 expected places; 47 admitted in 2026 (national admissions list).

Non-EU tuition at institution level: Set per programme and paid a full year in advance: EUR 17,300 per year for the engineering and IT programmes (Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Electronics, Engineering Innovation and Business, Interactive Technology Engineering, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Software Engineering, and the three BEng programmes) and EUR 15,000 per year for European Studies, Economics and Business Administration (Sønderborg) and Market and Management Anthropology. Application fee EUR 200 per applicant regardless of how many programmes you apply for. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay nothing.
